_comment: CARL built-in model catalogue. Downloaded and custom models are tracked separately in ~/.config/carl/models.json. Fields: hf (download source, pinned revision, sha256, bytes), tune (recommended server settings), why (the reason for each tuned value), ctx_zones (context per slot: <= good is fast (never below 96K, the floor), <= slow is usable, above very_slow is very slow; Auto-tune replaces these with measured values for this Mac), measured (reference measurements). Card fields: role (headline), good_for (tags: agent coding, hard code, chat & writing, uncensored), why_use, trade_offs, pick_instead (model + when), hardware, uncensored (what it means; abliterated models only), rank (quality order, 1 = best: parameters and density first, then quantization).

models.name: qwen3.6-35b-a3b
models.label: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B · Q4
models.summary: Default. Fast MoE: ~4x the decode and ~6x the prompt reading of the 27B, tiny KV cache.
models.description: Stock Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (not abliterated), unsloth dynamic Q4_K_M with the MTP head. Only 3B parameters are active per token, so decode is bandwidth-cheap (42-45 tok/s new text, 117 re-emitting code on an M3 Pro) and its KV cache is tiny (5.6 KiB/token at q4_0): two 96K slots cost under 1 GiB of KV. Thinking is on/off only (no effort levels). Needs a 32 GB+ Mac; 24 GB Macs get the IQ3 build.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP (n=2) + n-gram: measured best on Q4_K_M (M3 Pro): 42-45 tok/s new text vs 33 without speculation, 117 tok/s re-emitting code. The n-gram drafter copies repeated text (edits, file rewrites) almost for free.
why.ctx: 96K per slot: cold reads stay fast (64K reads at 229 tok/s, 128K at 117 tok/s on the M3 Pro). 128K-160K work with 8/8 recall but every cold re-read takes 4x longer.
why.slots: 2 slots: the main OpenCode session and a coder subagent each keep their own cache; the follow-up after a subagent takes 0.6 s instead of a full re-read.

models.why_use: The fastest good model: only 3B parameters work per token, so it writes ~4x faster and reads prompts ~6x faster than the 27B, and its tiny KV cache fits two 96K slots (main session + subagent) in under 1 GiB.
models.trade_offs: Weaker than the 27B on hard code (large refactors, subtle bugs, long reasoning); thinking is on/off only (no effort levels).

pick_instead.when: a task is too hard for it and you can wait (quality agent coding)

models.name: qwen3.8-27b
models.label: Qwen3.8 27B · Q4
models.summary: Stock dense 27B: slower (~11 tok/s) but stronger per token; effort levels for thinking.
models.description: Stock Qwen3.8-27B (not abliterated), unsloth dynamic Q4_K_M with the MTP head. Dense: every parameter is read for every token, so decode is ~11 tok/s and prompt reading ~85-90 tok/s. Same architecture and speed profile as the measured orcarouter build. Thinking supports effort levels (low/medium/xhigh, none = off). Its KV cache is 3x the 35B's (18 KiB/token at q4_0).

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP n=1 + n-gram: measured best on the dense 27B (10.5-11 tok/s new text vs 7.4 without, 27 tok/s re-emitting). n>1 loses on Metal for dense models: the extra draft verify costs more than it saves.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps (agents need that much context). On the 27B a cold read of a long session is slow (~56-65 tok/s at 66K: a full 96K window takes ~25 min), so windows above 96K are flagged as slow.
why.slots: 2 slots keep the main session cached while a subagent runs (1.9 s follow-up). Both generating at once time-share: no combined speed-up on dense models.

models.why_use: The strongest stock model in CARL: all 27B parameters work on every token, so it handles harder code and reasoning than the A3B, and thinking has effort levels (low / medium / xhigh). The choice for quality agent coding when you can accept the speed.
models.trade_offs: Slow: ~4x slower writing than the A3B and ~6x slower prompt reading (a cold read of a full 96K session takes many minutes); its KV cache is 3x the A3B's.

models.name: orcarouter-27b
models.label: orcarouter 27B · Q4 (abliterated)
models.summary: Abliterated 27B with published figures (0-2.7% refusals, MMLU +0.4). Fully measured.
models.description: orcarouter's abliterated Qwen3.8-27B, bartowski Q4_K_M with an imatrix calibrated on lots of tool calls, MTP head included. The only abliterated build with a documented method and published refusal and MMLU figures. Every CARL measurement of the 27B was made with this file.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP n=1 + n-gram: 10.5-11 tok/s new text, 27 tok/s re-emitting (none: 7.4). Measured with tools/llama-spec-sweep.sh on the M3 Pro.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps; cold reads at 66K run ~56-65 tok/s, so windows above 96K (flagged as slow) mean long waits after a restart or eviction.
why.slots: 2 slots: main session + subagent each keep their cache (1.9 s follow-up).

models.role: Uncensored quality coding and hard tasks
models.why_use: The same 27B as qwen3.8-27b with the refusal behaviour removed by a documented method (0-2.7% refusals, MMLU +0.4); its imatrix was calibrated with many tool calls. The only abliterated build CARL fully measured.
models.trade_offs: As slow as the stock 27B; never chosen automatically; a little larger than the stock Q4 (17.8 vs 16.5 GB).
models.uncensored: Uncensored: the refusal behaviour was removed from the weights (abliteration), so it answers requests the stock model declines, e.g. security research and exploit analysis, red-team prompts, frank medical, legal or drug questions, mature fiction. It adds no knowledge or skill and keeps the stock model's mistakes; you are responsible for how you use it.

models.name: qwen3.6-35b-a3b-iq3
models.label: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B · IQ3_XXS
models.summary: The 35B MoE in ~3-bit for 24 GB Macs. MTP + n-gram at n=1 (n=2 loses on IQ quants).
models.description: Stock Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, unsloth dynamic IQ3_XXS (~3-bit). Default on 24 GB Macs: 2 x 96K slots fit in ~15.3 GiB. IQ formats use lookup tables that unpack more slowly on Metal than K-quants; with only 3B active parameters decode is still fast (~45-50 tok/s on an M2 Max).

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP + n-gram, n=1. Measured on an M2 Max 32 GB (2026-10-03, llama.cpp 0.5.0, 400-token runs, mean of 2, tok/s prose/code/re-emit): none 49/45/46, MTP n=1 47/44/46, MTP n=2 40/41/49, n-gram 47/42/117, MTP+n-gram n=1 49/50/93, MTP+n-gram n=2 42/43/83. MTP alone adds nothing on IQ3 (the IQ kernels make the draft verify expensive) and n=2 costs ~15%; with n-gram at n=1 it is the best overall (n-gram alone wins only on re-emitting).
why.ctx: 96K per slot: the MoE KV cache is tiny, so long windows cost little memory; cold reads slow down past 128K.
why.slots: 2 slots fit even on 24 GB Macs: main session + subagent.

models.role: Everyday agent coding on a 24 GB Mac
models.why_use: Keeps the A3B's speed and two 96K slots in ~15 GiB, so subagents work on 24 GB Macs.
models.trade_offs: ~3-bit: less exact than the Q4, more mistakes in tool calls and edits.

models.name: qwen3.8-27b-iq3
models.label: Qwen3.8 27B · IQ3_XXS
models.summary: Smallest 27B (10.9 GB): for 24 GB Macs, or where nothing larger fits.
models.description: Stock Qwen3.8-27B, unsloth dynamic IQ3_XXS. The smallest 27B build: leaves room for a long window on 24 GB Macs. On 16 GB Macs the weights (10.2 GiB) exceed the default GPU limit (~10.7 GiB with buffers): it needs a raised limit (sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb). IQ3 unpacks slowly on Metal and loses more quality than Q3_K/Q4 in tool calls and edits; pick it only when nothing larger fits.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP + n-gram, n=1. Measured on an M2 Max 32 GB (2026-10-03, llama.cpp 0.5.0, 400-token runs, mean of 2, tok/s prose/code/re-emit): none 9.4/8.9/8.9, MTP n=1 9.7/9.8/11.0, MTP n=2 8.9/9.4/11.3, n-gram 9.8/9.6/21.5, MTP+n-gram n=1 10.0/9.8/31.1, MTP+n-gram n=2 8.7/9.7/23.3. MTP alone gains only ~5-10% on IQ3 (vs ~45% on Q4 on an M3 Pro); MTP+n-gram n=1 is best, n=2 loses.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps (agents need that much context). Dense 27B cold reads are slow, so windows above 96K are flagged as slow.
why.slots: auto: 2 slots when two windows fit.

models.why_use: The smallest 27B (10.9 GB): two 96K slots fit a 24 GB Mac, and with a raised GPU limit it can run on 16 GB.
models.trade_offs: ~3-bit IQ: the least exact 27B, more mistakes in tool calls and edits; slow (~10 tok/s on an M2 Max).
models.hardware: 24 GB Macs; 16 GB with a raised GPU limit
